item.title: Multimillion road contract
item.description: The people of Bogia and surrounding communities in Madang Province area are set to benefit from improved road access, following the signing of a multi – million kina contract, today. Governor General Sir Bob Dadae executed the 77million kina road contract between the Department of Works and Highways and Contractor Dekenai Construction Limited.
item.content:encoded:
The people of Bogia and surrounding communities in Madang Province area are set to benefit from improved road access, following the signing of a multi – million kina contract, today.

Governor General Sir Bob Dadae executed the 77million kina road contract between the Department of Works and Highways and Contractor Dekenai Construction Limited.

The signing was witnessed by Madang Governor Ramsey Pariwa and Bogia MP Robert Naguri.

The multi- million-kina contract covers the upgrading and sealing of 20 kilometers of the Madang coastal road from Nimbia to Bunapas.

Project is being funded under the government’s signature Connect PNG programe, specifically for the Momase Corridor.

Department of Works Secretary Gibson Holemba thanked the government for its continued funding of the program, saying improved road connectivity is vital for service delivery and economic development.

Madang Governor Pariwa said the road upgrade will open up economic opportunities for locals and neighboring East Sepik Province.

ICT Minister and Local MP Robert Naguri says he is proud that the long – awaited road upgrade and sealing would finally take place.

The 20 year Connect PNG initiative, is aimed at connecting key economic corridors including the Momase corridor linking Morobe, Madang, East Sepik and West Sepik.

item.title: To’o: Humbled to play in PNG
item.description: Playing international rugby league in Papua New Guinea is something many rugby league players anticipate. Whether you’re Australian, Kiwi, English, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Cook Islander, French or Lebanese, the passionate Papua New Guinean rugby league fan is unique.
item.content:encoded:
Playing international rugby league in Papua New Guinea is something many rugby league players anticipate.

Whether you’re Australian, Kiwi, English, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Cook Islander, French or Lebanese, the passionate Papua New Guinean rugby league fan is unique.

You find them no where else in the world, only in Papua New Guinea, a nation that calls rugby league its national sport.

Playing in front of passionate rugby league fans who support their team [PNG Kumuls] and also cheer on their favorite players playing against them is something many NRL and Super League stars anticipate when they play in PNG.

Samoan International, New South Wales Blues, Penrith Panthers and PNG Chiefs 2028 bound Brian To’o is keen on ticking that box come Saturday, when he runs out with Toa Samoa to face the PNG Kumuls.

After touching down in Port Moresby yesterday, the four-time NRL premiership winner said he is humbled to play in front of passionate fans.

“If I have to put down to one word, I would say beautiful,” To’o said

“Beautiful place, and I am very blessed and honored to be here. I am very grateful to be amongst the people of PNG and the Samoan community here.”

“Given that we will be playing in that special stadium [Santos NFS], I know that from past games I’ve watched.”

“You can see how much it means to the people, and how much they really adore the sport.”

“The only thing I can do to honor them is putting up my best performance this week against the brothers from the Kumuls.”

Despite having way more NRL players than the Kumuls, To’o said they won’t be taking the Kumuls lightly.

“They are a massive team, you can see that by the purpose they have when they play for their country.”

“They put up a massive performance against Lebanon last week and it is obviously going to be a massive challenge for us and we just have to be prepared to bring that intensity.”

item.title: Mangbil calls for accountability in El Nino response
item.description: Western Highlands Provincial Administrator and Chairman of the Provincial Disaster Committee, Joseph Iri Mangbil, has called on district administrators and finance managers to ensure transparency, accountability and proper use of disaster funds in responding to the El Nino situation. Mr. Mangbil made the call during an urgent provincial El Nino coordination meeting attended by district administrat
item.content:encoded:
Western Highlands Provincial Administrator and Chairman of the Provincial Disaster Committee, Joseph Iri Mangbil, has called on district administrators and finance managers to ensure transparency, accountability and proper use of disaster funds in responding to the El Nino situation.

Mr. Mangbil made the call during an urgent provincial El Nino coordination meeting attended by district administrators, district finance managers, LLG managers and the Provincial Finance Manager, police, electoral commission and international partners like UNDP, UNICEF, DFAT earlier this week.

The meeting discussed situational reports from the four districts, district El Nino response plans, financial arrangements, accountability and coordination of the provincial response.

Mangbil acknowledged that the K2.5 million allocated to each district for disaster response was insufficient to meet all the needs of communities affected by the El Nino situation.

However, he stressed that the limited funding made needs proper financial management, timely implementation and accountability.

“Honesty, transparency and accountability will play a major role at this crucial time. We need to work together to deliver services and support our people.”

The Provincial Disaster Chairman urged district authorities to manage the available funds responsibly and ensure that assistance reached the intended communities without unnecessary delays.

He said the provincial government, districts, local-level governments and relevant agencies must work together to coordinate their response and address the challenges facing the people.

" We will not engage casuals to do our work. We have to be responsible public servants and carry our work with due diligent so that our people must not be affected by this prolong Elnino," said Mr. Mangbil.

He also emphasised the importance of time management, calling on responsible officers to act promptly rather than allow delays to affect the delivery of essential assistance.

With communities facing the effects of El Nino, Mangbil said cooperation and responsible leadership were necessary to ensure that the limited resources available were used effectively.

He called on the district administrations and finance managers to take their responsibilities seriously and ensure that financial decisions and response activities were properly managed and accounted for.

The urgent meeting forms part of the province's efforts to coordinate district-level response plans and establish appropriate financial and administrative arrangements to address the El Nino situation in Western Highlands Province.

item.title: Kupo range fresh produce supplies to farmers

This is the third distribution from Kupo Range Fresh produce, a lead partner of the Fresh Produce Development
item.content:encoded:
While much of Simbu continues to feel the bite of the El Nino drought, the Kupo Range Fresh produce is planting hope by distributing seedlings, tools and farming materials to its 200 registered farmers and seven cluster groups from Kundiawa-Gembogl, Kerowagi and Gumine districts yesterday.

This is the third distribution from Kupo Range Fresh produce, a lead partner of the Fresh Produce Development Agency [FPDA] in Simbu, supported by the International Fund for Agricultural Development [IFAD].

Moses Gari the Acting Principal Advisor for the Division of Primary Industry [DPI] in Simbu, , commended Kupo Range for producing more farmers and creating market avenues.

David Kaupa the Provincial Coordinator for FPDA in Simbu, said Kupo Range continues to be the most impactful lead partner in the province because of its strict compliance.

“FPDA comes with high compliance. Any lead partner who complies, invests and shows discipline see positive results,” Kaupa said.

He said the PNG Government secured K54 million from IFAD in 2019 to start the project in five Highlands provinces including East New Britain and Madang for galip nut production.

In Simbu, FPDA profiled over 3,800 farming households across six districts – the highest in the country. Simbu first received K1.5 million worth of inputs during COVID-19, followed by K24 million.

“Agriculture is a sleeping giant. The Government has not realized its potential for 50 years, thanks to IFAD. Our ancestors lived on land and survived on agriculture. It is still our steppingstone to SME, to pay school fees, hospital bills and other costs” Kaupa said.

He said FPDA continues to support farmers, including solar-powered irrigation during this El Nino period, and urged farmers to treat farming seriously.

Francisca Moiwo, Director of Kupo Range Fresh Produce said phase One was valued at K71, 000, phase two at K91, 000 and phase three at K150, 000.

“The total support from the project in three phases is K223, 000, farmers’ own input is K66, 900, bringing total volume distributed to K289, 900 to 200 farmers and seven clusters group in three districts of Simbu,” she said.

Anna representing the farmers, expressed gratitude to Kupo Range, FPDA and IFAD.

“We thank Mrs. Moiwo and Kupo Range Fresh Produce for not forgetting us small farmers. These seedlings and tools will help us grow more food and earn money for our families,” Anna said.

“Before, we gardened only for food. Now FPDA and Kupo Range have taught us to farm as a business. We will not waste this support,” she added.

Mrs. Moiwo thanked DPI, FPDA and IFAD for their continued support towards food security and farmer empowerment in Simbu.

item.title: Koroba’s first FODE students to sit for National Examination
item.description: Koroba-Kopiago MP William Bando says he is encouraged to see initiatives that give young people a second chance in education. He said the registration of the Koroba District Flexible Open and Distance Education (FODE) Centre is an important step towards providing opportunities for those who have left school or missed out on formal education.
item.content:encoded:
Koroba-Kopiago MP William Bando says he is encouraged to see initiatives that give young people a second chance in education.

He said the registration of the Koroba District Flexible Open and Distance Education (FODE) Centre is an important step towards providing opportunities for those who have left school or missed out on formal education.

"Next Monday, first 120 students from Koroba District FODE will sit for their examinations. This is an important milestone for our district and a proud moment for these students, who have chosen to continue their education despite the challenges they have faced. I wish them all the best, together with other students across Hela Province and Papua New Guinea who will be sitting for their FODE examinations," Bando said.

The MP said recently when a young man in one of the WhatsApp groups he belongs to shared the examination parcel for the Koroba FODE Centre.

"Seeing this reminded me that many of our young people still have the desire to learn and improve their lives when given the right opportunities," he said.

Mr Bando said the district has committed funding to support school dropouts and those who could not continue their formal education.

"Our commitment to Pastoral Schools and alternative learning opportunities will continue because we believe every child and young person deserves a chance to learn, develop skills, and build a better future," he said.

He said FODE is a national government education program designed to widen access to education throughout Papua New Guinea. It provides a pathway for those who could not complete their schooling through the conventional system.

"Whatever circumstances forced you to leave school, do not give up on your education," Bando said.

He added that the Hela Provincial Government is also working towards establishing TVET centres to provide practical skills in areas such as business, carpentry, plumbing, and other trades.

"These opportunities can help our young people become self-reliant, establish small businesses, secure employment, and contribute to the development of their district, province, and country," he said.

"To our young people back home in Koroba and Lake Kopiago, I encourage you to find a FODE centre or school near you and explore the available opportunities to continue your education. If you left school because of family problems, financial difficulties, distance, or other circumstances, please do not lose hope. Education does not end when you leave the classroom. You can return to learning, acquire new skills, and create opportunities for yourself."

MP Bando also called on parents, community leaders, churches, and ward councillors to support young people to enrol in FODE and other available learning programmes in 2027.

"Let us also encourage those who are currently preparing for their examinations to remain focused, work hard, and do their best,” he said.

item.title: Man killed, school buildings torched in Irugl village
item.description: Several buildings were destroyed by fire at Irugl Village and a man was killed north of Denglagu Mission Station in Kundiawa-Gembogl District, Simbu Province, following an alleged domestic violence incident. The incident reportedly involved a man from Kerowagi District who was married to a woman from Irugl Village.
item.content:encoded:
Several buildings were destroyed by fire at Irugl Village and a man was killed north of Denglagu Mission Station in Kundiawa-Gembogl District, Simbu Province, following an alleged domestic violence incident.

The incident reportedly involved a man from Kerowagi District who was married to a woman from Irugl Village.

Madtin Tine, Director of Irugl Orphanage Centre, said the incident occurred at around 10 p.m. last night, about three kilometres from Denglagu Mission Station.

Mr. Tine said two houses were completely destroyed by fire, while two other houses, a double classroom building and a duplex teachers' residence were partially burnt.

"The alleged perpetrator, identified as Juth [name can be withheld], believed to be around 30 years old, was married to a local woman from Irugl Village. He reportedly travelled from Kerowagi District to Kundiawa-Gembogl in search of his wife after a domestic violence incident in their village in Kerowagi forced the woman to flee," Tine said.

He said in the course of searching for his wife, the man allegedly arrived at Irugl Village and set fire to buildings in the area before fleeing the scene.

However, witnesses indicated that youths later caught up with him at Gembogl Station that same night. The man allegedly attempted to attack those who confronted him and the situation escalated, resulting in his death.

Mr. Tine said the incident has raised serious concerns about the devastating consequences of domestic violence, the destruction of community property and the dangers of taking the law into one's own hands.

He said the destruction of homes and educational infrastructure is a significant loss for the affected families and the wider community.

"The damage to the double classroom building and the teachers' residence will disrupt education and affect the welfare of teachers and students," he said.

Police are expected to investigate the matter.

item.title: Resource companies test emergency response skills in Lae
item.description: Emergency response teams from Papua New Guinea’s major mining, oil and gas companies are testing their skills under pressure as the National Emergency Response Challenge (NERC) 2026 enters its second day in Lae. Hosted by the Mineral Resources Authority (MRA), the competition brings together emergency response teams from across the resource sector to demonstrate their capabilities in rescue operat
item.content:encoded:
Emergency response teams from Papua New Guinea’s major mining, oil and gas companies are testing their skills under pressure as the National Emergency Response Challenge (NERC) 2026 enters its second day in Lae.

Hosted by the Mineral Resources Authority (MRA), the competition brings together emergency response teams from across the resource sector to demonstrate their capabilities in rescue operations, firefighting, medical emergencies and incident management.

The 2026 challenge marks the competition’s return after a seven-year break, providing an opportunity for industry emergency responders to assess their readiness and learn from one another.

Harmony Hidden Valley Mine is among the participating companies, competing alongside Newmont Lihir, Barrick New Porgera, K92 Mining, New Simberi, Santos and Ramu NiCo.

The teams are being tested on their technical skills, leadership, decision-making and ability to work together during simulated emergency situations.

Harmony Hidden Valley Mine Safety, Health, Security and Risk Manager Mike Merena said the competition provides an important opportunity for emergency response personnel to measure their capabilities against industry peers and share practical knowledge.

“The National Emergency Response Challenge provides an excellent platform for our Emergency Response Team to showcase their skills, learn from other industry professionals and strengthen their ability to respond effectively to real-life emergencies.

“Our team works tirelessly to ensure the safety of our people, communities and operations. Participation in NERC reflects Harmony’s commitment to maintaining the highest standards of emergency preparedness and operational excellence.” Merena said.

He said the team’s participation reflects the company’s focus on training, skills development and operational readiness.

Beyond the competition, NERC provides a platform for emergency response professionals across the resource sector to exchange knowledge, share best practices and strengthen cooperation.

The challenge continues in Lae, with awards scheduled to be presented on Friday, October 23.

item.title: Luai: ‘My focus now is Samoa’
item.description: Jerome Luai will be calling Papua New Guinea home in 2028- but right now- his focus is doing well for Toa Samoa in the Rugby League World Cup. The Parramatta-bound play maker said this after touching down in Port Moresby, eyes fixed on playing against PNG Kumuls this Saturday at the Santos National Football Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
Jerome Luai will be calling Papua New Guinea home in 2028- but right now- his focus is doing well for Toa Samoa in the Rugby League World Cup.

The Parramatta-bound play maker said this after touching down in Port Moresby, eyes fixed on playing against PNG Kumuls this Saturday at the Santos National Football Stadium.

Despite a big 78-4 win over France last weekend, Luai says they won’t be taking the Kumuls lightly.

“With how the pool system is set up, we can’t afford to lose, and we are looking to face the Kumuls in a strong match, in front of their home crowd,” Luai said.

“They (Kumuls) are tough to beat in their home town.

“They (Kumuls) know how to adapt in such conditions so we’re looking forward to the challenge.”

Making it to the Rugby League World Cup final in the last edition, the former Penrith Panthers premiership winning five-eighth believes the current Toa Samoa team has the depth to go an extra mile.

“I think this team (Samoa) is much better than that team respectfully and we have a few tough games coming up so we have to be locked in in every game.” he added.

item.title: Wanuma people in Middle Ramu set to get road access
item.description: People in the newly created Wanuma Local Level Government of Middle Ramu District can now look forward to having road accessibility into the provincial capital after 51 years of being neglected by successive governments and leaders.
